H2.statement: cf beats fixed; margin grows with catalogue/rounds and tail weight

H3.statement: cf's advantage concentrates on rarely-seen workloads

H4.statement: machine count limits the achievable advantage

sanity.check: S1 matrices complete and strictly positive, no imputation
S2 oracle regret is exactly 1.000 in every condition
S3 no policy ever beats the oracle (regret >= 1.0 in every single run)
S4/S5 information containment and identical stream
S6 positive control: per_workload reaches the epsilon-greedy floor when rounds >> N x M
sanity.detail: per_workload 1.0355, exploration floor 1.0331, fixed 1.1299 at N=20, T=4000

sanity.check: S7 positive control: fixed converges to the offline best single machine

S9 random is strictly worse than fixed at T >= 2000
S10 seed spread reported for every number
sanity.detail: 8 seeds per condition, 40 for the T=60 conditions

sanity.check: S11 online cf does not beat the full-information fit of its own model class
